articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is titled "EPHEMERIS" and represents Volume 2, Number 10 of the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association, issued in October 1990. It serves as a periodical or newsletter for the association members.

articles.title: PULKOVO OBSERVATORY
articles.summary: This article announces the upcoming General Meeting featuring a presentation on Pulkovo Observatory by Lick Observatory historian Shilo Unruh. It also provides an update on subscription renewals for 'Astronomy' and 'Telescope Making' magazines, urging immediate action. The document also recaps a recent 'Equipment/Slide Night' showcasing advanced astronomical gear and photography, and lists a comprehensive schedule of October and November events including star parties, board meetings, and the AANC Conference.

articles.title: GET INTO BLACK HOLES FIGURATIVELY ONLY, PLEASE
articles.summary: Astronomer Andrew Fraknoi will present a non-technical lecture titled "Black Holes: Spacewarps, Time Machines, and the Death of Stars" at U.C. Berkeley on Saturday, November 3. The program, sponsored by U.C. Extension and the Astronomical Society of the Pacific, will run from 9 am to 5 pm and include illustrations from major telescopes.

articles.title: OCTOBER STARRY NIGHTS
articles.summary: This article outlines astronomical viewing opportunities and an important time change for October. It details the return to Pacific Standard Time on October 28th and offers observing notes for Mars, which will appear larger and enter retrograde motion. The "Challenge Object" for the month is Minowsky 92 (The Footprint Nebula) in Cygnus, with additional recommendations for binocular viewing of the Veil and North American nebulae, and the colorful double star Albireo.

articles.title: SPACE PROGRAM UPDATE
articles.summary: This space program update details the delayed Astro-1 Spacelab mission, designed to study hot stars and high-energy sources using various telescopes. It also reports on the Magellan probe, which, despite earlier communication issues, is now stable and returning high-resolution Venusian images while preparing for its mapping phase. Additionally, the article highlights new scientific data from the Hubble Space Telescope, successful Ariane 4 launches, and proposed changes to the Earth Observing System.

articles.title: SUPPORT - Sixty four Democratic and Republican senators signed a letter to Sen. Barbara Mikulski, chairman of a key appropriations panel, urging support for the international space station. The letter praised the program as a "catalyst for advancement" in education, science and the future economic health of the United States and said that the space station urgently needs consistent policy and funding support.
articles.summary: Sixty-four bipartisan senators urged support for the International Space Station (ISS), citing its importance for education, science, and the U.S. economy, and calling for consistent policy and funding while the program addresses technical issues like weight reduction and power management. The article also includes a review of "The Astronomer's Universe" by Friedman, which explores modern astrophysics, cosmology, and the history of technologically-based astronomy for a general educated audience.

articles.title: THE ASTRONOMY BOOKSHELF
articles.summary: This article is a review of Herbert Friedman's book, "The Astronomer's Universe," which comprehensively covers modern astrophysics and cosmology. The review highlights the book's structure, beginning with a detailed explanation of Space Age hardware and instrumentation across various wavelengths, before progressing to stellar phenomena, galaxies, and cosmological theories including the origin and fate of the universe and the search for extraterrestrial life. Friedman's ability to explain complex topics with clarity and balanced detail is particularly praised.

articles.title: METEOR NOTES
articles.summary: The article highlights October as an excellent month for meteor observations, featuring the year's fourth-best shower peaking near a new moon and numerous minor showers. It encourages observers to take advantage of this period before winter weather sets in, as the next good opportunity for minor shower activity won't be until April. Robert Lunsford (ALPO Meteors Recorder) provides further insights for the month.

articles.title: SIAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The SIAA Ephemeris details the upcoming peak of the Orionid meteor shower around October 21st, forecasting up to 30 meteors per hour under dark, moonless skies, with good visibility extending until October 24th. The article also notes potential activity from other minor showers and encourages observers to submit their meteor counts and photographs for inclusion in data sent to the American Meteor Society (AMS) and ALPO Meteors Section.

articles.title: INDIVIDUAL SHOWER NOTES:
articles.summary: This document provides individual notes on several meteor showers, including Kappa Cygnids, Annual Andromedids, October Draconids, Leo Minorids, Pegasids, and Delta Aurigids. It details their characteristics such as brightness, speed, radiant location, and associated comets. Special attention is given to the October Draconids, highlighting their historical strong outbursts and extremely narrow stream.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The article provides updates on cometary activity, noting Comet Levy's transition from an easy naked-eye evening object to a magnitude 7 morning object later in the year, and Comet Tsuchiya-Kiuchi's emergence into the morning sky for binocular observation. It also announces the recent passing of two prolific comet discoverers: John Bennett from South Africa (2 comets) and Minoru Honda from Japan (12 comets, 11 novae).

articles.title: SEEKING COMETS
articles.summary: This article, part of a "Seeking Comets" series, addresses common questions about the types and sizes of instruments amateur astronomers use for visual comet discovery, as well as the time commitment involved. It presents detailed tables of comets found with various reflectors and binoculars, listing discoverer, instrument specifications, comet magnitude, elongation, sky conditions, and discovery hours. The piece emphasizes that the observer, not just the instrument, is key to successful comet hunting.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS offers free advertising for non-commercial entities wishing to sell astronomy-related products or services. Submissions must be sent to the Editor, John P. Gleason, by the 15th of each month, and ads will run for approximately three months.

articles.title: TELESCOPES AND ACCESSORIES -
articles.summary: This document lists various used telescopes and accessories for sale, including a Meade 6-inch Schmidt-Newtonian telescope, several finderscopes (Telrad, Lumicon, Celestron), motors, adapters, filters, and a homemade 8-inch Newtonian optical tube assembly. Each item is described briefly with its condition and price.

articles.title: OFFICERS AND BOARD OF DIRECTORS | EPHEMERIS CONTRIBUTORS
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors of an organization, including positions like President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, Editor, and Director, along with their names and contact phone numbers. It also includes a separate list of individuals identified as "Ephemeris Contributors" with their contact information. The content serves as a directory of key personnel and contributors.

articles.title: COMET EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document provides detailed astronomical ephemeris data for three comets: Comet Levy (1990c), Comet Tsuchiya-Kiuchi (1990i), and Periodic Comet Encke. For specific dates in late 1990, it lists coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination for both 1950 and 2000 epochs), elongation from the Sun, sky visibility, and predicted visual magnitude to assist observers.

articles.title: THIS MONTH'S METEORS
articles.summary: The document provides an ephemeris for "This Month's Meteors," detailing several meteor showers with their key characteristics. It includes information on active dates, dates of maximum activity, maximum hourly rates, radiant points, velocities, and specific notes for observing. Notable showers like the Orionids, Southern Taurids, and Northern Taurids are featured with their respective peak rates and durations.

articles.title: Telescope and Equipment Listings
articles.summary: This document contains a comprehensive list of classified advertisements for used astronomical telescopes and equipment. It features various models from brands like Celestron, Meade, Televue, and Lumicon, including Newtonian, Schmidt-Cassegrain, and refractor telescopes, along with numerous accessories such as mounts, eyepieces, filters, and camera adapters. Each listing provides a description, price, condition, and seller contact information.

articles.title: Astronomical Society of the Pacific
articles.summary: The Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP) is an organization dedicated to advancing science and education, now in its second century of service. The document provides the society's contact information, including its address in San Francisco and phone number.

articles.title: Officers
articles.summary: This document lists the key officers of an organization, including the President, President-elect, Secretary, Treasurer, and Executive Director. Frank Drake is named President, with Julie H. Lutz as President-elect, John Gaustad as Secretary, Eugene Epstein as Treasurer, and Andrew Fraknoi as Executive Director, along with their institutional affiliations where noted.

articles.title: Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the members of a "Board of Directors," identifying each individual by name and their respective professional affiliation. The affiliations primarily include various universities, observatories, and other organizations, showcasing a diverse range of expertise on the board.

articles.title: At U.C. Extension Program with Andrew Fraknoi
articles.summary: Andrew Fraknoi will present a non-technical lecture titled "Black Holes: Spacewarps, Time Machines, and the Death of Stars" at U.C. Berkeley on Saturday, November 8. This all-day program, sponsored by U.C. Extension and the Astronomical Society of the Pacific, will cover various aspects of black holes, including their formation, interaction with stars, role in time travel, connection to quasars, and influence on science fiction.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION
articles.summary: This document is a membership application for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining different membership types, their costs, and instructions for submission. It includes the treasurer's mailing address and contact information for new or renewal applications. Additionally, it provides details about the SJAA's monthly publication, "EPHEMERIS," including submission guidelines and the editor's contact details.
